extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers / Royal Society readers (17th-century scientists); practitioners and readers of observational natural science
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing and reporting empirical observations and experiments in natural history and astronomy, including microscopy, dissections, astronomical timings, and remedies for animal disease. Emphasizes instrument specification, precise timing, drawings, comparative discussion with prior work, and detailed methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: State instruments and observational setup explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the instruments and their characteristics used for observations (e.g., 'a telescope that I have of about 24 feet', 'a tube of 16 feet', microscope), and note viewing conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Halley specifies a 24-foot telescope when observing Saturn's satellite; Flamsteed reports using a 16-foot tube to measure the moon's diameter. Include instrument type and dimensions so others can assess resolution and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record precise timings and correct clock references
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide exact times for events/observations and indicate how times were measured or corrected (e.g., 'times, by pendulum clocks, corrected').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: lunar eclipse phases listed with hours, minutes, seconds by different observers (Flamsteed, Halley, Haines). Use synchronized/corrected clocks and report times to the second where possible; tabulate phases and observers for comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give quantitative measurements with units and numerical detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Report measured values (distances, diameters, angular separations, counts, durations) numerically and with units or clear comparative statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Moon's diameter measured as '6702 = 33' 45"'; satellite periods computed in days/hours/minutes/seconds; blood/globule dissolution times given in fractions of a minute. Present raw numbers and derived quantities so others can reproduce calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe methods and procedural steps in enough detail for reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how samples/subjects were prepared, handled, and observed (e.g., straining brine through cloth, pricking a finger and mixing blood with salt, keeping flea eggs in a warm place).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: brine strained through eight folds of Holland and cambric; blood mixed in specific part ratios; flea eggs kept in a warm place and fed with part of a fly. Include amounts, ratios, timings, environmental conditions, and any special handling to allow replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report negative results and experimental limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: State unsuccessful attempts, limitations in keeping specimens, observational absences, and uncertainties (e.g., 'I could never yet see' certain satellites; 'I could keep them no longer alive than 11 days').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly note failures and plausible causes (steam on glass, unsuitable food, instrument limits). This helps interpret the reliability of positive results and guides future attempts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide drawings/figures scaled and detailed to show structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Include plates or drawings that represent specimens 'as large as nature' or magnified to show relevant details (e.g., muscle filaments, wing feathers, parts of plants occupying a whole sheet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: large copper cuts of plants 'generally as large as nature'; figures of flea filaments and gnat wings to show hairs and feathers. Label parts and give scale or magnification where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use microscopic observation and report microstructure details
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilize the microscope to describe fine structures (filaments, hairs, transparent plates, blood globules) and report counts, relative sizes, and observed changes over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: describing ring-like indentings in filaments, noting 'blood globules each to be dissolved into 6 distinct globules', observing oblong rectangular plates in brine. Give counts, relative proportions, and time-resolved changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare results to prior literature and reconcile discrepancies
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly compare observations with earlier authorities or observations (e.g., Huygens's numbers) and analyze differences quantitatively and qualitatively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Halley compares his satellite timings with Huygens, finds ~15° discrepancy in 20 years, discusses orbital eccentricity and proposes adjusted epoch and tables. Explain methods of comparison and consequences for theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show calculations and supply tables for derived quantities
rubrics_metrics.description: Present the arithmetic and tabular results used to derive periods, motions, and other computed values; include the intermediate steps and final tables where useful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Halley divides long time intervals by period to get number of revolutions and computes true period; states derived diurnal and annual motions and composes tables (not printed here). Provide the math so readers can verify the derivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterize lifecycle and developmental timings with observational detail
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting life-history observations (eggs → larvae → nymph → adult), record durations, developmental changes, feeding conditions, and behavioral notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: flea eggs hatched in 4 days; worms lived up to 11 days; nymphae moved on the 4th day and broke their case on the 10th. Report feeding trials and environmental factors affecting survival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe sample preparation and filtration effects explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: When filtering or straining samples (e.g., brine), report the filter media, pore fineness, and what was retained or passed through, and interpret microscopic findings in relation to the filtration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: brine strained through many folds of Holland and cambric left only black dust; microscope showed rectangular oblong plates and animalcules that passed through cloth. Note cloth pore relative sizes vs particles observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide practical stepwise remedies and containment methods for disease reports
rubrics_metrics.description: In accounts of epizootics or remedies, give step-by-step treatments, composition/ratios of antidotes, and recommended containment/prevention measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: for murrain—examine tongue for aphthae, rub until it bleeds, wipe with new unwashed linen, apply lotion of salt and good vinegar; antidote composed of soot, gunpowder, brimstone, salt in equal parts with water; prevent spread by immediate separation, fumigation of stalls, cleanliness, ventilation, and inoculation. Include dosing where given (e.g., 'a large spoonful for a dose').

rubrics_metrics.name: Use comparative anatomy and distinguishing characters to support classification
rubrics_metrics.description: List distinguishing morphological or anatomical features (numbers, shape, organs) that justify taxonomic or functional claims about species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: describing Lumbricus Latus features—flatness, peculiar joints, many mouths (one in every joint), and internal organs; distinguishing univocal generation with separate sexes vs hermaphroditism in other worms. Present comparative lists of features to support claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide ratios, concentrations and time-dependent reaction observations for chemical/biological mixes
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting small-scale chemical/biological reactions, state proportions used (e.g., two parts blood to one part salt), describe immediate color changes, and record dissolution or reaction times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: blood with salt turned 'immediately of a more lively red' and blood globules dissolved into six distinct globules; with four parts salt to one of blood some globules dissolved wholly in 1/2 minute. Report exact ratios and timepoints to document kinetics.
